neet_che_u12_t05_1.working: In an octahedral field the t2g set points between the ligands, so it is stabilised and sits at -0.4Δo. The eg set rises to +0.6Δo.

neet_che_u12_t05_2.working: A weak field gives the high-spin configuration t2g3 eg1. CFSE = 3(-0.4) + 1(0.6) = -0.6Δo, with no extra pairing energy.

neet_che_u12_t05_4.working: A: Δo > P gives low spin t2g4 (II). B: Δo < P gives t2g3 eg1 (I). C: the lower set in a tetrahedral field is e (IV). D: the highest orbital in square planar is dx2-y2 (III).

neet_che_u12_t05_5.working: A is true: Δo rises from 3d to 4d to 5d. B is true: Δt is small, so tetrahedral complexes are high spin. C is false: F- is a weaker-field ligand than H2O. D is false: CFT treats ligands as point charges, so it cannot explain CO being strongest. E is true: higher oxidation state gives larger Δo. Correct set is A, B and E.
